# Terms of the external target schemes

## 1. What this file is for

The milestone for the external mappings does not start with a table. It starts
here. Before one line is written that puts a requirement from the ISO world
beside an identifier from a foreign scheme, what that scheme permits has to be
evidenced. Without this entry the first table works on an assumption.

Two sentences from the plan decide it here. Given away free of charge does not
mean free of rights. And what is known in advance is no working basis as long as
it is not evidenced. Until then the strictest reading holds, and an unevidenced
yes is a no.

This file reproduces no terms. It names, per scheme, the address that was read,
the date of the reading, and summarises in our own words what stands there.
Anyone who needs the wording calls up the address.

## 2. Our own licence as the yardstick

The original material of this repository is under CC-BY-SA-4.0. That licence
permits commercial use and requires passing on under the same licence.
Everything that comes in here has to be passable on under those conditions.

That is the point where two of the three schemes fail, regardless of how
generous their terms are otherwise. A condition that rules out commercial use
cannot be reconciled with CC-BY-SA-4.0, because passing on under the same
licence would open that use up again.

## 3. What an identifier is and what it is not

The sections below separate two things, because they are not the same question.

A bare identifier is a reference, so `ORP.1`, `PR.AA-01` or `4.1`. This
repository has pointed at foreign documents by standard, clause and edition
since its first commit and reproduces no text. That is the copyright boundary in
`copyright/en.md`, and it holds for a framework the same way it holds for an ISO
standard. So being allowed to carry an identifier follows from our own boundary
and not from a permission granted by the foreign scheme.

Everything else is content: the heading belonging to an identifier, the text
behind it, the order and the structure of the catalogue, an adopted selection.
That needs a permission, and the sections below say per scheme whether there is
one.

Where a no stands below, it is a no to the content. It is not a no to a line
that names an ISO requirement and puts an identifier and a sentence of our own
reasoning beside it.

## 4. BSI IT-Grundschutz

**Read:** `https://www.bsi.bund.de/DE/Service/Nutzungsbedingungen/Nutzungsbedingungen_node.html`,
on 2026-08-05.

**Conditions of release.** Software and publications offered as a free download
may be used for non-commercial purposes only. IT-Grundschutz material may be
altered within that use in order to implement internal security measures; other
material of the office stays unaltered. Quotation is possible without consent
where sense and context are preserved, the wording stands in quotation marks and
the source is named.

**What is explicitly not permitted.** Commercial use and use for advertising
without prior written consent. Mirroring the content without prior written
consent. Using the name of the office as a reference without consent. Use of the
logo, which is protected as a state emblem. Any impression of a collaboration
with the office or of an official site. Framing the pages inside a foreign
frame.

**May the identifiers be carried in a table?** Yes, as a bare reference, so the
building block identifier such as `ORP.1` and nothing further. That follows from
section 3 of this file and not from a permission by the office; the terms that
were read say nothing about identifiers.

**May the content be carried?** No. The terms permit the free publications for
non-commercial purposes only, and this repository passes everything on under
CC-BY-SA-4.0, which includes commercial use. The two do not go together. No
heading of a building block, no requirement number with its text, no adopted
structure and no adopted selection.

**Under what attribution.** A table carrying identifiers names the office as the
publisher of the scheme, names the edition of the compendium and the address,
and says that the mapping is our own reading and does not come from the office.
That last sentence is not a courtesy; it follows from the ban on creating the
impression of a collaboration.

**What that means for the table.** It is possible, but narrow. It carries the
identifier, our own reasoning and the ISO side of the line. What a building
block requires stands in our own words or not at all.

## 5. NIST Cybersecurity Framework

**Read:** `https://www.nist.gov/open/copyright-fair-use-and-licensing-statements-srd-data-software-and-technical-series-publications`
and `https://www.nist.gov/oism/copyrights`, both on 2026-08-05. The current
version is CSF 2.0, carried as NIST CSWP 29 at
`https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.CSWP.29`, read on the same day.

**Conditions of release.** Works authored by employees of the institute are not
subject to copyright protection within the United States; rights outside the
United States are expressly reserved. Independently of that, the page that was
read expressly grants the public a non-exclusive, perpetual, paid-up and
worldwide right to reprint the works in every format, in all subsequent editions
and in derivative works. A reprint carries the line the institute states for it.
For images and text on the web pages a credit is requested.

The worldwide reach of that grant is the decisive sentence here. The reservation
of rights outside the United States on its own would have left no working basis
for a repository that is read from Germany.

**What is explicitly not permitted.** Nothing may create the impression that the
institute recommends or endorses something. On name, logo and testing symbol
nothing was readable on this route: the page carrying that question answers with
404, and the command stands below. So nothing is established about logo and
testing symbol, and under the strictest reading that means no. No logo, no
testing symbol, no use of the name beyond naming it as the source.

**May the identifiers be carried in a table?** Yes. Functions and categories
such as `GV.OC-01` or `PR.AA-01` are references, and section 3 holds for them.

**May the content be carried?** Yes, within the granted permission and with the
stated attribution. This is the only one of the three schemes where the text may
be more than a reference. Whether the repository makes use of that is a
different question: our own copyright boundary asks for our own words, and it is
stricter than what would be permitted here. The boundary stays the working rule.

**Under what attribution.** The line the institute states for a reprint, plus
the reference with designation and edition, and a sentence saying that the
mapping is our own reading and does not come from the institute.

## 6. CIS Controls

**Read:** `https://www.cisecurity.org/terms-of-use-for-non-member-cis-products`,
on 2026-08-05.

**Conditions of release.** The controls and the documents belonging to them are
under the Creative Commons Attribution-Non Commercial-No Derivatives 4.0
International Public License. Copying and redistributing as a framework for
non-commercial purposes is permitted, with credit to the publisher and a link to
the licence. Anyone citing the controls is asked to point at
`cisecurity.org/controls/`, so that the current version is the one meant.
Commercial use requires the prior approval of the publisher.

**What is explicitly not permitted.** Distributing altered material. That is the
part of the licence which allows no derivative works, and it hits a mapping
table directly: a table that re-sorts or condenses the content of the controls
is exactly that. Beside it, commercial use without prior approval.

**May the identifiers be carried in a table?** Yes, as a bare reference, so
`5.1` or `CIS Control 5` and nothing further, per section 3 of this file.

**May the content be carried?** No, and it fails in two places at once. The
licence rules out commercial use, our own material is under CC-BY-SA-4.0 and
allows it. And the licence allows no derivative works, while a mapping does
nothing other than re-order foreign material. No heading, no text of a control,
no adopted order.

**Under what attribution.** A table carrying identifiers names the publisher,
the version of the controls, the address `cisecurity.org/controls/` and says
that the mapping is our own reading.

## 7. What follows from this for the three tables

The same build holds for all three, and it is narrower than the one somebody
would have built without this entry. A line carries the ISO side, the identifier
of the target scheme, the kind of relation and one or two sentences of our own
reasoning. It carries no heading and no text from the target scheme.

More would be permitted for the institute's framework. The table stays with the
same build all the same, so that the three tables have one form and nobody
argues from one to the others.

## 8. What is not checked here

Whether the terms have changed since 2026-08-05. Anyone building a table reads
the addresses again and writes their own date into the table.

Whether there are further terms beside the addresses that were read belonging to
the same documents. What was read per scheme is the page carrying the terms, and
for the institute's framework the general copyright page as well. A licence
agreement that can be entered into with the office or with the publisher of the
controls was not examined, because this repository has none.

Whether a bare identifier is unprotected in every jurisdiction. Section 3 rests
on this repository's own copyright boundary and not on a statement from the
three houses. None of the three says anything about identifiers on the pages
that were read.

Whether the ban on creating the impression of a collaboration asks for anything
beyond the attribution rules above. That is a question for the office and not
for a web page.

## 9. The commands

That the page on the institute's name and testing symbol cannot be read:

```
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" --max-time 20 -A "Mozilla/5.0" https://www.nist.gov/nist-logo-and-testing-symbol
404
```

That the three addresses that were read answer:

```
for u in \
  https://www.bsi.bund.de/DE/Service/Nutzungsbedingungen/Nutzungsbedingungen_node.html \
  https://www.nist.gov/open/copyright-fair-use-and-licensing-statements-srd-data-software-and-technical-series-publications \
  https://www.cisecurity.org/terms-of-use-for-non-member-cis-products ; do
  printf '%s ' "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 25 -A 'Mozilla/5.0' "$u")"; echo "$u"
done
200 https://www.bsi.bund.de/DE/Service/Nutzungsbedingungen/Nutzungsbedingungen_node.html
200 https://www.nist.gov/open/copyright-fair-use-and-licensing-statements-srd-data-software-and-technical-series-publications
200 https://www.cisecurity.org/terms-of-use-for-non-member-cis-products
```
